Shakuntala.note: Daughter of the sage Vishvamitra and the apsara Menaka, raised by the sage Kanva; wife of Dushyanta and mother of Bharata.

Brahma.name: Brahma Dev
Brahma.note: The self-born creator, source of every lineage in this tree: from his mind-born sons spring the devas, the sages, the rakshasas and, through them, the kings of both the solar and the lunar dynasties.

Marichi.note: A mind-born son (Prajapati) of Brahma; father of Kashyap.

Atri.note: A mind-born son of Brahma, one of the Saptarishi; father of Chandra (Soma).

Daksha.note: A Prajapati; father of the many wives of Kashyap, and so grandfather of the devas, nagas, birds and much else.

Kashyap.note: The great progenitor rishi; by his many wives, father of the devas (Adityas), the asuras, the nagas and the birds.

Saraswati.note: Goddess of speech and wisdom, consort of Brahma; mother of his mind-born sons.

Bhrigu.note: A mind-born son of Brahma, a Prajapati and Saptarishi; father of Shukracharya, guru of the asuras.

Vasishtha.note: A mind-born son of Brahma, chief of the Saptarishi and family priest of the Ikshvaku kings; forefather of the line of Parashara and Vyasa. By name — the long rivalry with Vishvamitra, sparked when Vishvamitra coveted his wish-fulfilling cow Nandini/Kamadhenu and was refused; all hundred of his sons killed by Vishvamitra's curse, after which he tried and failed to end his own life by fire, water and cliff, each element refusing to harm him; the Trishanku and Harishchandra quarrels that turned him and Vishvamitra into birds fighting for years; cursing King Saudasa into the rakshasa Kalmashapada, then fathering his heir on Kalmashapada's queen Madayanti by niyoga after the king's death; and a later son, Shakti, father of Parashara and so grandfather of Vyasa.

Shakti.note: Son of Vasishtha and father of Parashara; of the Vasishtha line.

nakAshvini.name: Ashvini
nakAshvini.note: One of the twenty-seven nakshatras, daughters of Daksha and wives of Chandra.

Vajrangi.name: Varangi
Vajrangi.note: Wife of Vajranga; mother of Tarakasura.

Anasuya.note: Wife of Atri, a paragon of virtue; mother of Dattatreya, Durvasa and Chandra.

Dattatreya.note: Son of Atri and Anasuya, born because she prayed for an incarnation. He gave the teaching of transcendence to Alarka, to Prahlada and to Kartavirya Arjuna, all three of whom stand in this tree, and the mystic perfections he gave Kartavirya are what made that king unkillable by anyone but Parashurama. The sixth of the avatars, SB 1.3.11.

Durvasa.note: Son of Atri and Anasuya; the wrath-swift sage whose boon gave Kunti her deva-sons.

Agastya.note: The pot-born sage, son of Mitra and Varuna; who drank the ocean, humbled the Vindhya, and digested the asura Vatapi. Husband of Lopamudra.

Arundhati.note: Wife of Vasishtha; the star Alcor, paired with him as the archetypal devoted couple.

Puloma.note: Wife of Bhrigu; mother of Chyavana and Shukracharya.

Dhatri.note: One of the twelve Adityas, sons of Kashyap and Aditi. SB 6.6.

Amsha.note: One of the twelve Adityas, sons of Kashyap and Aditi. SB 6.6.

Kamadeva.note: God of love, mind-born of Brahma. (Later reborn as Pradyumna, Krishna’s son.)

people.Rati: Goddess of desire; daughter of Daksha, wife of Kamadeva. Sources disagree on her mother: most simply call her Daksha's daughter, but one tradition holds she was born of Daksha's own perspiration, without a mother at all -- so, unlike her sisters, she is not attached to Prasuti here.

Gargya.note: A brahmin of Garga's line, mocked as impotent by Syala in the Yadava assembly. He went to the western sea and lived twelve years on iron filings until Shiva granted him a son who would break the Yadavas. HV 58; VP 5.23

Ajigarta.note: A starving brahmin who sold his middle son to be Harishchandra's sacrifice, and took a further fee to hold the knife himself. SB 9.7.20; AB 7.13-16

Shunahshepha.name: Shunahshepha (Devarata)
Shunahshepha.note: Bought by Rohita to die in his place, he praised the devas from the stake until his bonds fell away. Vishvamitra adopted him as Devarata, god-given, over the protests of his own sons. His brothers were Shunahpuccha and Shunolangula. SB 9.7.20-26; AB 7.13-18

Shunahpuccha.note: Eldest son of Ajigarta, whom his father would not sell. AB 7.15

Shunolangula.note: Youngest son of Ajigarta, whom his mother would not give. AB 7.15

Kanva.note: Son of Apratiratha, kshatriya-born and a brahmin by life. He found the infant Shakuntala in the forest where Menaka had left her, brought her to his ashram and raised her; it was under his roof that Dushyanta met her. SB 9.20.6-11

Medhatithi.note: Son of Kanva; his sons, headed by Praskanna, were all brahmins. SB 9.20.7

Dirghatamas.note: The blind sage of the Rigveda, son of Mamata and Utathya, and by Bali's queen the father of Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Suhma, Pundra and Odra: six kings and six kingdoms of the east. His own son by the maid Ushij was Kakshivan. SB 9.23.5; RV 1.140-164

Narada.note: The third of the avatars, SB 1.3.8. Mind-born son of Brahma, who walks through every age of this tree and sets half of it moving: he sends Kalayavana at Mathura, curses Kubera's sons into a pair of trees, teaches Dhruva and Prahlada, and gathers the parts of the Veda that are about devotion alone. SB 1.3.8

Sanaka.note: Eldest of the four Kumaras, the first of the avatars: Brahma's mind-born sons, who refused to father anything and stayed four boys for ever, in a vow of celibacy older than the world. SB 1.3.6, 3.15

Sananda.note: One of the four Kumaras, the first of the avatars. SB 1.3.6

Sanatana.note: One of the four Kumaras, the first of the avatars. SB 1.3.6

Sanatkumara.note: One of the four Kumaras, the first of the avatars. SB 1.3.6

KratuRishi.name: Kratu
KratuRishi.note: Mind-born son of Brahma, one of the Saptarishi; married Kriya, daughter of Kardama and Devahuti. Not the Yadava Kratu, son of Krishna and Jambavati.

Pulaha.note: Mind-born son of Brahma, one of the Saptarishi; by his wife Kshama, father of Kardama (among others), and so grandfather of Kapila. Vishnu Purana 1.10.

Atharva.note: Mind-born son of Brahma, eponym of the Atharvaveda; married Shanti (here ShantiAtharva), daughter of Kardama and Devahuti.

Kardama.note: Son of Pulaha and Kshama, per Vishnu Purana 1.10; husband of Devahuti, father of Kapila and of eight daughters married to the other eight of the nine sages. Not Brahma's own son, and not on his row: the tree follows Pulaha's own generation for him, one below Brahma. SB 3.24 for Devahuti, Kapila and the daughters.

Devahuti.note: Daughter of Svayambhuva Manu; wife of Kardama; mother of Kapila and of eight daughters married to eight of the nine sages. Taught Sankhya by her own son. SB 3.24-33.

Kala.note: Daughter of Kardama and Devahuti; wife of Marichi. SB 3.24.15.

ShraddhaAngirasa.name: Shraddha
ShraddhaAngirasa.note: Daughter of Kardama and Devahuti; wife of Angiras, so grandmother of Brihaspati. Not Shraddha, wife of Vaivasvata Manu. SB 3.24.16.

Havirbhu.note: Daughter of Kardama and Devahuti; wife of Pulastya. SB 3.24.17.

Kriya.note: Daughter of Kardama and Devahuti; wife of Kratu. SB 3.24.19.

Khyati.note: Daughter of Kardama and Devahuti; second wife of Bhrigu, alongside Puloma. SB 3.24.20.

ShantiAtharva.name: Shanti
ShantiAtharva.note: Daughter of Kardama and Devahuti; wife of Atharva. Not Shanti, son of Krishna and Kalindi. SB 3.24.22.

Chitragupta.note: Born from Brahma's own body after eleven thousand years of meditation, and from that body -- kaya -- the Kayasthas take their name. Yama's recorder: he keeps the ledger of every deed of every being, and it is read back at the judgement in Yamaloka, which is the whole of his fame and none of it kinship, so no edge joins him to the deva he serves six rows below. GP 2.5

Dadhichi.note: Son of Atharva and Shanti. The devas came to him when Vritra could not be killed by anything made, and asked for his bones; he gave up his body on the spot by yoga and Vishvakarma cut the vajra out of his spine, which is the one weapon that worked. In the Rigveda he is Dadhyanc, who knew the madhu-vidya and was forbidden by Indra to teach it on pain of losing his head — so the Ashvins took his head off, set a horse's head on him, learned it from that mouth, and put his own head back. SB 4.1.42, 6.9-10; RV 1.116.12, 1.117.22; MBh 3.98

SuvarchaD.name: Suvarcha
SuvarchaD.note: Wife of Dadhichi. She was carrying Pippalada when her husband gave his body away for the thunderbolt, and the child was taken living from her. Skanda and Bhavishya Puranas; not in the Bhagavata's account.

Pippalada.note: Son of Dadhichi and Suvarcha, born after his father was already dead of it and raised, the story says, under a pipal tree — which is where the name comes from. He is the teacher of the Prashna Upanishad: six seekers come to him with fuel in their hands, he tells them to stay a year first, and then answers the six questions, of which the last is what it is that knows. Prashna Upanishad 1; Bhavishya Purana

unions.note: Prasuti confirmed as mother of 41 of these children (all but Rati, whose parentage stays unconfirmed -- see u_daksha_rati) via SB 6.6 (direct verse lookup) and, for Danayus and Khasa, the Vishnu Purana's naming of Panchajani -- the same figure this tree treats as Prasuti -- as their mother. Formerly split across this union (mother unconfirmed) and a separate childless u_daksha_prasuti; merged into one real union rather than left duplicated. SB 4.1.2's sixteen daughters by Prasuti and SB 6.6's sixty are, under this tree's single-Daksha reading, the same event told two ways, not two broods.

Diti, having lost two sons to Vishnu, kept a year-long vow to bear one who would kill Indra. Indra waited on her, served her, and the night she slept with her feet where her head should have been he went into her by yoga and cut the embryo with the vajra into seven, and each of the seven into seven again. Every piece cried and would not die; and because they cried he said ma rodih, do not weep, and made the forty-nine his own companions instead of his death. The Puranas name the seven courses of the wind and not the forty-nine, so seven records stand here for all of them. SB 6.18.53-78; MBh 1.65
Garga's son was Shini and Shini's son Gargya, kshatriya-born and brahmin by practice. SB 9.21.31

Nine daughters given to the nine sages on Brahma's instruction, and Kapila, the ninth-avatar son. Anasuya (already wed to Atri) and Arundhati (already wed to Vasishtha) are the two of the nine already in the tree; this is the union that gives them a mother and father. SB 3.24.
SB 3.24.20. A second, earlier union alongside Bhrigu's marriage to Puloma.
SB 3.24.22 for the marriage; SB 4.1.42 for the son.

Wikipedia's Pulaha article gives this (via Vishnu Purana 1.10, Pulaha and Kshama's sons Kardama, Urvarivat, Sahishnu); the tree adopts it on request. Distinct from the tradition that has Kardama arise directly from Brahma's own shadow (SB 3.12); the Bhagavata's own genealogy is not overridden, just not the one followed here.

Rati stays on her own union, mother unconfirmed: most sources call her Daksha's daughter without naming which wife, and at least one tradition (see her own note) has her born of Daksha's own perspiration, no mother at all. Not merged into u_daksha with her sisters, whose mother is now confirmed as Prasuti.
Skanda Purana. The Bhagavata gives Dadhichi no wife and no son.
